brief.analysis: Defense is undergoing a genuine spending-regime shift (NATO/Europe rearmament and rising global military budgets), and the data confirms the drift directly: detrended_z of 0.97 versus raw z of 1.92 shows the ratio is barely stretched against its own rising trend. ma_score is 0/3 with an intact 50DMA, and the 200DMA is already essentially met (+2.2%), so the +20.4% target to the 5-year mean is a stale center that the trend has left behind. The 5-year mean is not a valid target.
brief.report_line: Short ITA/SPY to the 5-year mean: avoid, because the detrended z (0.97 vs 1.92 raw) shows the defense-spending regime has lifted the ratio's trend and the flat mean overstates the stretch.

brief.analysis: The AI capex cycle is a live structural regime shift lifting semiconductors' share of the Nasdaq, with SMH gaining ~82% in a half-year and equipment makers and non-Nvidia names now participating — this is exactly the secular index-share change that invalidates an old mean. The +65.9% distance to the 5-year mean, ma_score of only 1/3, and an intact 50DMA slope all say the ratio's center of gravity has permanently risen; the 5-year mean is not a valid target. The +13.7% 200DMA target is the only defensible reversion here, and even that fights a strong trend.
brief.report_line: Short SMH/QQQ at 2.67z: engine-flagged but we avoid the 5-year-mean thesis because the AI capex regime has structurally re-rated semiconductor index share, making the old mean a statistical trap rather than a magnet.

brief.analysis: The strongest regime argument is silver's structural industrial demand (solar, electronics, clean energy) layered on gold's own central-bank bid, which can hold the ratio above its old mean; but with peak z of 6.36 already collapsed to 0.98, detrended_z of just 0.53, and the 200DMA already achieved, most of the dislocation has resolved. The remaining +13.5% push to the 5-year mean is a real but low-conviction leg — tradeable if sized down, not a clean reversion. The mean may have drifted modestly higher, so treat the 5-year target as optimistic.
brief.report_line: Short SLV/GLD residual to the 5-year mean: size down, as the 200DMA is already hit and silver's industrial-demand regime argues the ratio's floor has risen, capping downside.

brief.analysis: Metals and miners carry a real structural tailwind from record gold and strong silver/copper demand, and the readings confirm the reversion has largely played out: current z is only 0.65, detrended_z is -0.12 (no stretch left on a trend basis), and the 200DMA is already achieved after a 4.57 peak. The perfect 2/2 base rate and 3/3 ma_score are constructive, but the residual +10.7% push to the 5-year mean fights a commodity regime that may have raised the ratio's floor. Tradeable on the base rate, but size down and lean on the 200DMA, not the 5-year mean.
brief.report_line: Short XME/SPY residual: the reversion is nearly complete (200DMA hit, detrended z ~0), so we take the base-rate edge in reduced size while flagging the metals-demand regime as a cap on the final leg to the 5-year mean.
